def-transient-maxwell-system-with-materi:
## Definition

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded Lipschitz polyhedron, or a periodic rectangular cell. The real electric field is $E(t,x)\in\mathbb R^3$ and the magnetic flux density is $B(t,x)\in\mathbb R^3$; the magnetic intensity is $H=\mu^{-1}B$. Let $\epsilon(x)$ and $\mu(x)$ be measurable, time-independent, symmetric matrix fields for which there are constants $0<\epsilon_0\le\epsilon_1$ and $0<\mu_0\le\mu_1$ with
$$\epsilon_0|v|^2\le v^T\epsilon(x)v\le\epsilon_1|v|^2,\qquad \mu_0|v|^2\le v^T\mu(x)v\le\mu_1|v|^2$$
for almost every $x$ and every $v\in\mathbb R^3$. A conductivity tensor $\sigma(x)$, when present, is measurable, symmetric, and positive semidefinite. The coefficients may jump across finitely many Lipschitz material interfaces. No derivative of a coefficient is part of the model.

In each material region the constitutive fields satisfy
$$\partial_t(\epsilon E)=\operatorname{curl}(\mu^{-1}B)-J_{\rm src}-\sigma E,\qquad \partial_t B+\operatorname{curl}E=0.$$
Here $J_{\rm src}$ is the impressed free-current density, while $\sigma E$ is the conductive current. Electric charge $\rho$ is constrained by $\operatorname{div}(\epsilon E)=\rho$ and the total-current continuity equation $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(J_{\rm src}+\sigma E)=0$; the magnetic constraint is $\operatorname{div}B=0$. These equalities are distributional. In the lossless branch set $\sigma=0$.

The boundary choice is one of the following. A **periodic boundary** identifies opposite traces of the rectangular cell. A **perfect electric conductor (PEC) boundary** imposes zero tangential trace $n\times E=0$ on $\partial\Omega$. At a material interface with no singular surface charge or current, the weak equations are understood with the transmission conditions $[n\times E]=0$, $[n\cdot B]=0$, $[n\times(\mu^{-1}B)]=0$, and $[n\cdot(\epsilon E)]=0$, where $[q]$ is the trace from one side minus the trace from the other. The interface conditions are part of the model convention; no smooth Taylor expansion across a coefficient jump is asserted.

For PEC, the weak Ampere equation is $(\epsilon E_t,v)_{L^2}-(\mu^{-1}B,\operatorname{curl}v)_{L^2}=-(J_{\rm src}+\sigma E,v)_{L^2}$ for every $v\in H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$ as defined in [[def-na-zero-tangential-hcurl]]; the periodic branch uses periodic $H(\operatorname{curl})$ test fields. Faraday’s equation remains $B_t+\operatorname{curl}E=0$ in distributions. These weak forms define the test-space and boundary convention used by the edge finite element method.

The weighted field norms are $\|E\|_\epsilon^2=\int_\Omega E^T\epsilon E\,dx$ and $\|B\|_{\mu^{-1}}^2=\int_\Omega B^T\mu^{-1}B\,dx$. The uniform coefficient bounds make them equivalent to the ordinary $L^2$ norms. All later smooth-error claims require smoothness separately on each mesh-aligned material region.
lem-maxwell-rectangular-stokes-identity:
## Statement

Let $F=\{(x_0,y,z):y_0\le y\le y_1,\ z_0\le z\le z_1\}$ be an oriented rectangle with normal $e_x$, and let $E$ be a $C^1$ vector field near $F$. Orient $\partial F$ by the outward-normal-first convention. Then
$$\int_{\partial F}E\cdot t\,ds=\int_F(\operatorname{curl}E)\cdot e_x\,dS=\int_{y_0}^{y_1}\int_{z_0}^{z_1}(\partial_yE_z-\partial_zE_y)(x_0,y,z)\,dz\,dy.$$
The identities for normals $e_y$ and $e_z$ follow by cyclic permutation of coordinates. Reversing a face orientation reverses both integrals.
def-maxwell-discrete-cochain-and-yee-gri:
## Definition

Let $K$ be a finite oriented three-dimensional cell complex with vertex, edge, face, and volume cochains. An edge cochain records oriented electric line integrals, a face cochain records oriented magnetic fluxes, and a vertex cochain records electric charge. Write $N_v,N_e,N_f,N_c$ for the retained vertex, edge, face, and cell counts. On a periodic cell, identify opposite cells with orientation preserved and let $G,C,D$ be the full vertex-to-edge gradient, edge-to-face curl, and face-to-cell divergence incidence matrices, each the transpose of its signed oriented boundary matrix. For a PEC closure, “interior” means not in the boundary subcomplex. Keep only interior electric edges as unknowns and only interior vertices as volume-charge locations, but keep all face fluxes, including boundary-normal magnetic fluxes, and all cells. This closure has no separate boundary surface-charge cochain. Define $G$ and $C$ by restricting the absolute vertex-edge and edge-face incidence matrices to those rows and columns. This mixed closure imposes zero tangential electric edge cochains on the boundary while allowing a fixed normal magnetic flux on boundary faces. In both cases, $G\in\mathbb R^{N_e\times N_v}$, $C\in\mathbb R^{N_f\times N_e}$, and $D\in\mathbb R^{N_c\times N_f}$ satisfy $CG=0$ and $DC=0$.

The electric, magnetic, and conductive material matrices are real symmetric matrices $M_e\in\mathbb R^{N_e\times N_e}$, $M_b\in\mathbb R^{N_f\times N_f}$, and $S\in\mathbb R^{N_e\times N_e}$, respectively. The first two are positive definite and represent the discrete weighted inner products induced by $\epsilon$ and $\mu^{-1}$; $S$ is positive semidefinite and represents conductivity. Write $\langle e_1,e_2\rangle_{M_e}=e_1^TM_ee_2$, $\langle b_1,b_2\rangle_{M_b}=b_1^TM_bb_2$, and $\|e\|_{M_e}^2=\langle e,e\rangle_{M_e}$, $\|b\|_{M_b}^2=\langle b,b\rangle_{M_b}$. In a homogeneous isotropic periodic Cartesian grid with spacings $h_x,h_y,h_z$ and cell volume $V=h_xh_yh_z$, the diagonal entries for an $x$-edge and an $x$-normal face are $\epsilon V/h_x^2=\epsilon h_yh_z/h_x$ and $\mu^{-1}h_x/(h_yh_z)$; the $y$ and $z$ entries are obtained by cyclic permutation. These values are dual-volume Hodge weights for line-integral and face-flux cochains. A compatible PEC closure uses the corresponding truncated dual volumes for free electric edges, while the magnetic mass includes boundary faces; the resulting matrices remain positive definite. The discrete constraints are $G^TM_ee^n=\rho^n$ on interior vertices and $Db^{n-1/2}=0$ on all cells.

For current cochains $j^{n+1/2}$ and charge rows $\rho^n$, the discrete continuity condition means
$$\rho^{n+1}-\rho^n+\Delta t\,G^T\left(j^{n+1/2}+S\frac{e^{n+1}+e^n}{2}\right)=0.$$
For PEC this is the interior-vertex volume-charge relation; this closure has no separate boundary surface-charge/current cochain.

The cochain identities $CG=0$ and $DC=0$ are not imposed as an extra numerical approximation: they follow from oriented boundary-of-boundary cancellation, including the PEC row and column restrictions, as proved in [[lem-maxwell-discrete-incidence-identities]]. No cell geometry picture is used as a proof.
lem-maxwell-discrete-incidence-identitie:
## Statement

For the incidence matrices $G,C,D$ of [[def-maxwell-discrete-cochain-and-yee-grid]], one has $CG=0$ and $DC=0$. The conclusion holds for the full periodic complex and for the PEC mixed closure defined there.
lem-maxwell-yee-step-matrix-is-positive-:
## Statement

Let $M_e$ be the positive definite electric mass matrix, let $S$ be the positive semidefinite conductivity matrix, and let $\Delta t>0$. Then $M_e+(\Delta t/2)S$ is symmetric positive definite, hence invertible. Thus each midpoint-conductivity Yee electric row has a unique solution.
alg-maxwell-yee-leapfrog-update:
## Definition

Choose a finite complex and boundary closure as in [[def-maxwell-discrete-cochain-and-yee-grid]], step size $\Delta t>0$, initial $e^0\in\mathbb R^{N_e}$ and $b^{-1/2}\in\mathbb R^{N_f}$, and source rows $j^{n+1/2}\in\mathbb R^{N_e}$. The output is a sequence $e^n$ at integer times and $b^{n+1/2}$ at half-integer times. For each $n\ge0$, perform the ordered instructions

1. Update the face flux by
   $$b^{n+1/2}=b^{n-1/2}-\Delta t\,C e^n.$$

2. Solve the electric row
   $$\left(M_e+\frac{\Delta t}{2}S\right)e^{n+1}=\left(M_e-\frac{\Delta t}{2}S\right)e^n+\Delta t\,C^TM_b b^{n+1/2}-\Delta t\,j^{n+1/2}.$$

For $S=0$ this is the lossless Yee leapfrog scheme. For $S\succeq0$, the midpoint term is the specified trapezoidal treatment of conductivity. The row is well defined for every input because its matrix is invertible by [[lem-maxwell-yee-step-matrix-is-positive-definite]]. This procedure makes no stability claim; the lossless stability condition is proved separately.
thm-maxwell-yee-gauss-constraints-propag:
## Statement

For the Yee update in [[alg-maxwell-yee-leapfrog-update]], suppose the initial rows satisfy $G^TM_e e^0=\rho^0$ and $Db^{-1/2}=0$. If the source and charge rows satisfy
$$\rho^{n+1}-\rho^n+\Delta t\,G^T\left(j^{n+1/2}+S\frac{e^{n+1}+e^n}{2}\right)=0$$
at every step, then $G^TM_e e^n=\rho^n$ and $Db^{n-1/2}=0$ for every later step. This is exact constraint propagation; it does not assert stability for a time step violating the CFL condition.
thm-maxwell-yee-strict-cfl-modified-ener:
## Statement

Set $K=C^TM_bC$ and
$$\lambda_{\max}:=\max_{e\ne0}\frac{e^TKe}{e^TM_ee}.$$
For a lossless, source-free update from [[alg-maxwell-yee-leapfrog-update]], define
$$\mathcal E^n:=\frac12(e^n)^TM_ee^n+\frac12(b^{n-1/2})^TM_bb^{n+1/2},\qquad b_c^n:=\frac{b^{n-1/2}+b^{n+1/2}}2.$$
Then $\mathcal E^n$ is independent of $n$, and
$$\mathcal E^n\ge\frac12\left(1-\frac{\Delta t^2\lambda_{\max}}4\right)\|e^n\|_{M_e}^2+\frac12\|b_c^n\|_{M_b}^2.$$
Consequently, the actual strict spectral condition $\Delta t^2\lambda_{\max}<4$ makes this modified energy positive on admissible staggered states and controls the electric field and the centered magnetic field. When $\lambda_{\max}>0$, at equality the energy loses coercivity and a maximal mode has a repeated root $-1$; above equality a mode grows exponentially. If $\lambda_{\max}=0$, the strict condition is automatic for every $\Delta t>0$ and neither endpoint case occurs.
thm-maxwell-yee-cartesian-dispersion-and:
## Statement

Consider a homogeneous isotropic periodic Yee grid with $\epsilon,\mu>0$, wave speed $c=(\epsilon\mu)^{-1/2}$, spacings $h_x,h_y,h_z$, and $N_x,N_y,N_z$ cells. Its allowed wave angles are $\theta_j=2\pi m_j/N_j$. On a mode with wave vector $k_j=\theta_j/h_j$, the transverse curl-curl eigenvalue is
$$\lambda(\theta)=c^2\sum_{j\in\{x,y,z\}}\frac{4}{h_j^2}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta_j}{2}\right),$$
and the lossless Yee leapfrog dispersion relation is
$$\sin^2\left(\frac{\omega\Delta t}{2}\right)=c^2\Delta t^2\sum_{j\in\{x,y,z\}}\frac{\sin^2(\theta_j/2)}{h_j^2}.$$
The exact finite-grid strict condition is $\Delta t^2\max_{\theta}\lambda(\theta)<4$, as in [[thm-maxwell-yee-strict-cfl-modified-energy]]. The rectangular sufficient bound is
$$\Delta t<\frac{1}{c\sqrt{h_x^{-2}+h_y^{-2}+h_z^{-2}}};$$
it is exact when every $N_j$ is even. For a cubic grid this bound is $\Delta t<h/(c\sqrt3)$. Odd cell counts may have a smaller finite-grid maximum, so the finite-grid eigenvalue is the exact criterion.
lem-maxwell-periodic-yee-consistency:
## Statement

Let a periodic rectangular cell be discretized by a uniform Cartesian Yee grid with spacings $h_x,h_y,h_z$, $h=\max_jh_j$, and constant scalar coefficients $\epsilon,\mu>0$. Let $(E,B)$ be a source-free smooth periodic Maxwell solution on $[0,T]$, with the spatial derivatives of $E$ through total order four, $\partial_t^4E$, and $\partial_t^3B$ bounded. Sample $E(t_n)$ by exact oriented edge line integrals $e_*^n$ and $B(t_{n+1/2})$ by exact oriented face fluxes $b_*^{n+1/2}$. Define
$$r_h^n=M_e\frac{e_*^{n+1}-2e_*^n+e_*^{n-1}}{\Delta t^2}+C^TM_bCe_*^n,\qquad s_h^n=b_*^{n+1/2}-b_*^{n-1/2}+\Delta t\,Ce_*^n.$$
With the homogeneous diagonal Hodge weights of [[def-maxwell-discrete-cochain-and-yee-grid]], there is a constant $C_T$ independent of the cell counts such that, whenever $\Delta t\le t_n\le T-\Delta t$,
$$\|r_h^n\|_{M_e^{-1}}\le C_T(h^2+\Delta t^2),\qquad \|s_h^n\|_{M_b}\le C_T\Delta t^3.$$
Here $\|r\|_{M_e^{-1}}^2=r^TM_e^{-1}r$. This is a smooth homogeneous periodic consistency result; it asserts no Taylor estimate across coefficient jumps or a PEC boundary closure.
thm-maxwell-periodic-yee-smooth-solution:
## Statement

Assume the hypotheses and residual bounds of [[lem-maxwell-periodic-yee-consistency]] on $[0,T]$. Write $\delta_{tt}u^n=(u^{n+1}-2u^n+u^{n-1})/\Delta t^2$. Let $e_h^n,b_h^{n+1/2}$ be a lossless periodic Yee solution and let $e_*^n,b_*^{n+1/2}$ be the exact samples. Set $w^n=e_h^n-e_*^n$ and $z^{n+1/2}=b_h^{n+1/2}-b_*^{n+1/2}$. Suppose the initial electric rows are compatible with the Yee equations and satisfy
$$\|w^0\|_{M_e}+\|Cw^0\|_{M_b}+\|w^1\|_{M_e}+\|Cw^1\|_{M_b}+\left\|\frac{w^1-w^0}{\Delta t}\right\|_{M_e}+\|z^{1/2}\|_{M_b}\le C_0(h^2+\Delta t^2).$$
Let $\lambda_{\max}$ be the largest generalized curl-curl eigenvalue in [[thm-maxwell-yee-strict-cfl-modified-energy]]. If the strict spectral margin obeys $\gamma:=1-\Delta t^2\lambda_{\max}/4\ge\gamma_0>0$, then for every integer $n\ge0$ with $t_{n+1}\le T$,
$$\|e_h^n-e_*^n\|_{M_e}+\|b_h^{n+1/2}-b_*^{n+1/2}\|_{M_b}+\|C(e_h^n-e_*^n)\|_{M_b}\le C(h^2+\Delta t^2),$$
where $C$ is independent of the grid counts and time step. The statement is for the smooth homogeneous periodic branch and compatible starts; it makes no Taylor error claim across material jumps or an unspecified PEC boundary stencil.
thm-maxwell-yee-midpoint-conductivity-en:
## Statement

For the midpoint-conductive update of [[alg-maxwell-yee-leapfrog-update]], define the same staggered cross-energy as in [[thm-maxwell-yee-strict-cfl-modified-energy]]. Then for every step
$$\mathcal E^{n+1}-\mathcal E^n=-\Delta t\left(\frac{e^{n+1}+e^n}{2}\right)^Tj^{n+1/2}-\Delta t\left(\frac{e^{n+1}+e^n}{2}\right)^TS\left(\frac{e^{n+1}+e^n}{2}\right).$$
With zero impressed current, this algebraic energy is nonincreasing because $S\succeq0$. Under the strict spectral CFL hypothesis of [[thm-maxwell-yee-strict-cfl-modified-energy]] it is also positive on admissible update states. Dissipation is asserted for this specified midpoint treatment, not for an arbitrary conductivity discretization.
def-maxwell-edge-fem-semidiscretization:
## Definition

Let $\Omega$ be a bounded contractible Lipschitz polyhedron with a finite matching affine tetrahedral mesh $\mathcal T_h$, and use the real lowest-order spaces $W_h^0,N_h^1,N_h^2,N_h^3$ defined in [[def-na-lowest-order-whitney-de-rham-spaces]]. The electric trial field is $E_h(t)\in N_h^1\cap H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$; the magnetic flux field is $B_h(t)\in N_h^2$, with no imposed zero normal trace on $B_h$. PEC means the closure-defined zero tangential subspace from [[def-na-zero-tangential-hcurl]]. Periodic analogues use the periodic cell complex. Countable Choice is inherited from the H(div) and affine Piola space definitions in the suppliers; the finite matrix operations below use no additional choice.

For edge basis $\{\phi_i\}$ and face basis $\{\psi_a\}$, define the symmetric mass matrices
$$ (M_e)_{ij}=\int_\Omega \phi_j^T\epsilon\phi_i\,dx,\qquad (M_b)_{ab}=\int_\Omega \psi_b^T\mu^{-1}\psi_a\,dx.$$
They are positive definite by the coefficient bounds in [[def-transient-maxwell-system-with-material-interfaces]] and linear independence of the finite element bases. Let $C$ and $D$ be the coefficient matrices of $\operatorname{curl}:N_h^1\to N_h^2$ and $\operatorname{div}:N_h^2\to N_h^3$ in the oriented edge, face, and cell moment bases; the moment-commuting supplier gives $DC=0$. Set $j_i(t)=\int_\Omega J_{\rm src}(t)\cdot\phi_i\,dx$, with $J_{\rm src}\in C([0,T];L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$. The lossless, conductivity-free semidiscretization with this source is
$$M_e\dot e-C^TM_b b=-j,\qquad \dot b+Ce=0.$$
This is a spatial Galerkin system only; no time integrator is included. The cochain convention and weak material-interface formulation come from the declared spaces and [[def-transient-maxwell-system-with-material-interfaces]]. Smooth interpolation and a uniformly bounded commuting projection are separate prerequisites for the later error estimate and are not asserted by this definition.
lem-maxwell-finite-dimensional-ode-exist:
## Statement

Assume the Countable Choice branch inherited from [[def-maxwell-edge-fem-semidiscretization]]. For any finite matching mesh, initial edge and face coefficients $(e_0,b_0)$, and continuous load vector $j:[0,T]\to\mathbb R^{N_e}$, the source-driven semidiscrete Maxwell system
$$M_e\dot e-C^TM_bb=-j(t),\qquad \dot b+Ce=0,\qquad (e(0),b(0))=(e_0,b_0)$$
has one and only one global $C^1$ solution on $[0,T]$. The construction and uniqueness argument use finite-dimensional linear algebra and the matrix-ODE supplier; no choice axiom stronger than the inherited Countable Choice branch is used.
thm-maxwell-edge-fem-energy-conservation:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice only as inherited from the real $H(\operatorname{div})$/Piola finite-element space interfaces in [[def-maxwell-edge-fem-semidiscretization]]. For the lossless source-free semidiscretization
$$M_e\dot e-C^TM_b b=0,\qquad \dot b+Ce=0,$$
the weighted energy
$$\mathcal H_h(t)=\frac12\|e(t)\|_{M_e}^2+\frac12\|b(t)\|_{M_b}^2$$
is constant in time. The local matrix calculation uses no further choice principle.
def-maxwell-edge-ritz-projection:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice in the inherited edge/face finite-element space branch. Let $V=H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$ with the PEC convention in [[def-maxwell-edge-fem-semidiscretization]], and let $V_h=N_h^1\cap H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$. Define
$$m(u,v)=\int_\Omega v^T\epsilon u\,dx,\qquad a(u,v)=\int_\Omega (\operatorname{curl}v)^T\mu^{-1}\operatorname{curl}u\,dx,\qquad a_+(u,v)=m(u,v)+a(u,v).$$
For $u\in V$, the **Maxwell curl-energy Ritz projection** $R_hu\in V_h$ is the solution of
$$a_+(R_hu,v_h)=a_+(u,v_h)\qquad(v_h\in V_h).$$
Its finite-dimensional well-definedness, orthogonality, and best-approximation property are supplied by [[lem-maxwell-edge-ritz-projection-well-defined]].
lem-maxwell-edge-ritz-projection-well-de:
## Statement

In the Countable Choice branch of [[def-maxwell-edge-ritz-projection]], the equation defining $R_hu$ has a unique solution for each $u\in V$. Moreover, with $\|v\|_{a_+}^2=a_+(v,v)$,
$$\|u-R_hu\|_{a_+}\le\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_{a_+}.$$
lem-maxwell-nedelec-smooth-interpolation:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice only in the H(div)/Piola space branch inherited from the suppliers below. Let $\mathcal T_h$ be a finite matching affine tetrahedral mesh of a bounded polyhedron, with shape-regularity constant $\sigma$ and $h=\max_K h_K$. Assume material interfaces are mesh-aligned. Let $u,v$ be piecewise $C^1$ on cell closures, with $\operatorname{curl}u$, $\operatorname{div}v$ also piecewise $C^1$, and with matching tangential traces of $u$ and matching normal traces of $v$. The canonical edge and face moment interpolants $I_h^1,I_h^2$ are those in [[lem-na-whitney-moments-commute-with-grad-curl-div]]. Then
$$\begin{aligned} &\|u-I_h^1u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|\operatorname{curl}(u-I_h^1u)\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \quad+\|v-I_h^2v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|\operatorname{div}(v-I_h^2v)\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \le C_\sigma h |\Omega|^{1/2}\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\left(\|\nabla u\|_{L^\infty(K)}+\|\nabla\operatorname{curl}u\|_{L^\infty(K)}+\|\nabla v\|_{L^\infty(K)}+\|\nabla\operatorname{div}v\|_{L^\infty(K)}\right). \end{aligned}$$
The constant depends only on reference-element basis norms and $\sigma$. This estimate is only for the canonical smooth-input interpolants; it makes no boundedness claim on all of $H(\operatorname{curl})$ or $H(\operatorname{div})$.
lem-maxwell-magnetic-compatible-initial-:
## Statement

Assume the contractible Lipschitz domain and shape-regular mesh-family hypotheses of [[thm-na-uniformly-bounded-commuting-cochain-projection]], with matching affine tetrahedra and the PEC edge space of [[def-maxwell-edge-fem-semidiscretization]]. Assume Countable Choice as in that projection interface. Let $B_0\in H(\operatorname{div};\Omega)$ be piecewise smooth, have matching normal traces, and satisfy $\operatorname{div}B_0=0$. Let $\pi_h^2$ be the degree-two cochain projection in that interface, let $X_h=\operatorname{range}C\subset N_h^2$, and let $P_{X_h}$ be orthogonal projection onto $X_h$ for $(u,v)_{\mu^{-1}}=\int_\Omega u^T\mu^{-1}v\,dx$. Define
$$B_h^0=\pi_h^2B_0+P_{X_h}(B_0-\pi_h^2B_0).$$
Then $B_h^0\in N_h^2$, $D B_h^0=0$, and
$$(B_h^0-B_0,\operatorname{curl}v_h)_{\mu^{-1}}=0\quad(v_h\in V_h),\qquad \|B_h^0-B_0\|_{\mu^{-1}}\le C h\,M_B,$$
where $V_h=N_h^1\cap H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$ and $M_B$ is the maximum of the piecewise first-derivative bounds for $B_0$ and $\operatorname{div}B_0$ used by the smooth interpolation estimate. The error constant is uniform over the shape-regular family when the commuting projection norms are uniformly bounded.
thm-maxwell-edge-fem-smooth-solution-err:
## Statement

Let $\Omega$ be a bounded contractible Lipschitz polyhedron with a shape-regular family of matching affine tetrahedral meshes, maximum diameter $h\to0$, and mesh-aligned material interfaces. Let $\epsilon,\mu$ be time-independent symmetric uniformly positive definite bounded coefficients. Let $(E,B)$ be a PEC solution of [[def-transient-maxwell-system-with-material-interfaces]] with $J_{\rm src}\in C^1([0,T];L^2(\Omega)^3)$, satisfying the stated current continuity and magnetic divergence constraints. Assume $E,E_t,E_{tt}$ are piecewise $C^1$ in space, their curls are piecewise $C^1$, and their tangential traces match across interior mesh faces and vanish on the exterior PEC boundary; assume $B(0)$ is piecewise $C^1$ with matching normal traces and $\operatorname{div}B(0)=0$. These bounds are uniform in time on $[0,T]$.

Take the semidiscrete solution of [[def-maxwell-edge-fem-semidiscretization]] with exact load moments, initialize $E_h(0)=R_hE(0)$ using the Maxwell Ritz map of [[def-maxwell-edge-ritz-projection]], and initialize $B_h(0)=B_h^0$ by [[lem-maxwell-magnetic-compatible-initial-projection]]. Write $\theta_h(t)=E_h(t)-R_hE(t)$. The Countable Choice assumption required by that projection interface is in force. Then the semidiscrete solution exists uniquely and
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}\left(\|E_h(t)-E(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|\operatorname{curl}(E_h(t)-E(t))\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|B_h(t)-B(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\right)\le C_T h.$$
The constant depends on $T$, the coefficient bounds, the shape-regularity and projection bounds, and the stated piecewise smooth norms, but not on $h$. The initial magnetic projection preserves the discrete divergence constraint, and its error $B_h^0-B(0)$ is $\mu^{-1}$-orthogonal to all discrete curls. The result is a PEC semidiscrete estimate for smooth mesh-aligned data; it does not claim a rate across unresolved jumps or for nonsmooth fields.
